issue.title: A [fresh::] stamp lands on a closed Pomodoro ledger line and becomes part of its theme name

task_type_fields.impact:
Every theme consumer (Stats Themes panel, `bob themes` catalog, plan budget, Recent
suggestions, and the planned Day strip theme lane) sees a bogus theme and splits that day's
VIBE minutes in two. Pomodoro ledger lines must never carry freshness stamps. Fix the stamper
guard; whether name parsing should also ignore inline `[field:: …]` runs is a separate call.
task_type_fields.location: bob-plugins Pomodoro reopen/status gesture (suspected task-status-cycler) writing [fresh::] onto ## Pomodoros lines; vault 2026/20261025.md:38
task_type_fields.repro:
Vault commit `dcbe953f` (kellys-mbp, 2026-10-25 10:36:47 -0400) changed the closed Pomodoro
line `- [x] (**1020-1035** [t:: 15m]) — VIBE` in `2026/20261025.md` to
`- [ ] (**1020-1035** [t:: 15m]) — VIBE [fresh:: 2026-10-25]`, stripped the 🍅 marks from
its six Task Link children, and in the same commit moved three linked `sase.md` tasks from
`[/]` to `[*]`. That looks like a Pomodoro reopen gesture (suspected: the bob-plugins
task-status-cycler Pomodoro reopen path) running a generic `fresh` stamper on the ledger
line itself. The line was later re-closed and still carries the stamp
(`git -C ~/bob log -S"VIBE [fresh:: 2026-10-25]" -- 2026/20261025.md`).

Second symptom: Stats reads the stamp as part of the Pomodoro name.
`bob stats show worked -a -f json -g day -r 2026-10-25..2026-10-25` reports a theme part
`VIBE [FRESH:: 2026-10-25]` (15m) beside `VIBE`, and `theme_hues` gains a
`vibe [fresh:: 2026-10-25]` entry with its own hash hue.

issue.creation_reason: Found while sizing the Day strip theme lane against live Stats data: a Pomodoro line carries a fresh stamp, which pollutes theme names.
